status: diagnostic-only; Gate C failed, so Gate D cannot pass
technical: Seed 29 repeats both final frames byte-for-byte. All three seeded target-layout digests reproduce and non-target guards match; no page/shader errors captured.

findings.defect: Seed 41 overfills near framing and hides the open middle
findings.evidence: Tall near grass and very large close boulders dominate the eye-height image.
findings.hypothesis: Fixed world-zone ranges do not account sufficiently for terrain-relative projected size, occlusion and local rising ground.
findings.recommendation: A future parent-dressing plan needs screen-projected-size/occlusion constraints computed once into stable world anchors, with terrain slope/height checks. Do not implement a screen vignette.

findings.defect: Exposed distant-landform underside in seed 41 inspection
findings.evidence: A light horizontal mass floats above a strip of sky near the upper right/center.
findings.cause: Existing sphere-based distant landform and finite ground do not form a continuous landscape for every seeded terrain.
findings.recommendation: A later coordinated terrain-continuation representation is needed; no approved geology rule is established by recoloring the old shape.

findings.defect: Strip-like vegetation and smooth generic stone persist across seeds
findings.evidence: Both extra seeds retain broad directional growth but close detail is geometric and stones lack convincing weathered structure.
findings.recommendation: Do not promote the fibre/rock implementations globally or claim that changing seed fixes their artistic defects.

betterThanOriginal: Material continuity and removal of opaque fragmented clutter improve in the tested presentation, but the full style and robustness remain inadequate.
sharedLearning: Seeded determinism is not compositional robustness. Keep rules R5/R6/R7/R8 proposed; record these images as counterexamples to assuming good seed-29 framing generalizes.
